newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent trades at Oct -10 cts, could fall more.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent trades at Oct -10 cts, could fall more.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude took a tumble on Monday and could fall further, traders said.
A Sept 19-21 Brent cargo traded on Monday at October Brent -10 cents, down from Friday's deal at Oct -7 cents and sellers saw few interested buyers remaining.
"I can't see anything to stop it going to (October) -15 cents when it might work to the States," one trader said.
The arbitrage to the U.S. narrowed by 15 cents on Monday.
Most other North Sea sweet grades were pretty well cleared to the end of the month and not expected to lose much ground.
A Sept 27-29 Forties cargo moved at a steady Dated Brent +36 cents.

Oseberg was one of the exceptions with a somewhat pressured cargo available around the 20th of the month. A Gullfaks C (Sept 18-20) was heard traded at a low dated Brent +15 cents. Ekofisk saw only five September cargoes -- all with month end options.

Apart from Gullfaks, which undergoes some maintenance in October, production from other North Sea crudes was expected unchanged to slightly firmer. Some expected October Brent output to be as high as 50 cargoes -- from 44.8 in September.
Intermonth spreads eased slightly over the afternoon with Oct/Nov trading at +67 cents and recent talk at +64/67. while Nov/Dec slipped to +59/61 cents.
Mediterranean crude rallied on strong downstream demand and continued loading delays at Russia's Novorossiisk terminal in the Black Sea.
Russia's Urals was valued at Dated Brent -85/75 cif Augusta, 10 cents above one week ago.
Berthing at Novorossiisk was suspended over the weekend due to bad weather, exacerbating the existing 5-6 day delay due to pipeline maintenance in September, dealers said.
Some traders emphasised the importance of these delays in the recent price rise, and another said it was mostly linked to the recent surge in gas oil prices.
But another said: "It's more to do with the strength of high sulphur fuel oil in the Med."
